comment: Noticing rules — pure data (the DECISIONS side), evaluated client-side by src/explainer/evaluateRules.js. Same shapes/ops as the first proof (ssi-learning-app/tools/explainer/rules.json): node | perChild | countWhere; ops eq/gt/lt/gte/lte/truthy/falsy/daysSinceGt. `source` distinguishes compile-time pack.snapshot data from runtime page payloads. Invitations, not missions — see docs/self-explaining-popty.md §5.
joinConvention: For a perChild rule with source:'snapshot', the evaluator resolves each array item's snapshot slice by the item's own identifying field before testing itemWhen — e.g. rule 'known-vocab-flags' below evaluates itemWhen against { ...item, ...pack.snapshot.vocabGate[item.code] }. This is a plain per-item join, not a new op. For a node rule needing a course-set membership test (rule 'recorder-pending-recording'), the mount resolves one boolean (`courseFlags.isHumanVoiceCourse = pack.truth.voicePolicy.humanVoiceCourses.includes(route.courseCode)`) once, before invoking the rule engine — again no new op, just a field the mount adds to its own evaluation context. Both conventions are documented here rather than silently assumed; see the report for why an 'in' op was deliberately NOT added.
